description: The conditional functions defined in terms of CASE short-circuit: only the selected branch is evaluated, which is what makes the standard guard idiom work - IFF(x IS NOT NULL, f(x), NULL) must not call f on the NULL rows, and NVL(a, g(b)) must not compute the fallback when a is non-NULL. Evaluating every argument first made such guards fail on exactly the rows they were written to exclude, so each test puts 1/0 in the branch that must not run. Includes the vendor idiom end to end (a Java UDF that rejects NULL, guarded by IFF), a check that ordinary results are unchanged, and the arity rule: COALESCE needs at least TWO arguments, live-verified, while GREATEST(1) and LEAST(1) are fine. Converted 1:1 from functions/ConditionalShortCircuitTest (now retired).

steps.sql: SELECT IFF(s IS NOT NULL, strict_len(s), NULL) AS n FROM guard_src ORDER BY n

SELECT IFF(x > 2, 'big', 'small') AS label, COALESCE(NULL, x, 99) AS c, NVL(NULL, x * 2) AS d
FROM (SELECT 1 AS x UNION ALL SELECT 5) ORDER BY x
